items.title: Avoidance of a compact set by bounded-energy holomorphic spheres is open
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be a compact smooth manifold, $J_0$ a smooth almost complex structure, $K\subset X$ compact, and $E_0<\infty$. Suppose the image of every nonconstant $J_0$-holomorphic sphere is disjoint from $K$.

There are a $C^\infty$ neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of $J_0$ among smooth almost complex structures on $X$ and an open neighborhood $V$ of $K$ such that every nonconstant $J$-holomorphic map $u:\mathbb {CP}^1\to X$ with $J\in\mathcal U$ and energy $E_g(u)\le E_0$ has image disjoint from $V$. Neighborhoods can be restricted by any additional fixed auxiliary constraints on $J$ simply by intersection.

More precisely, if $J_n\to J_0$ smoothly, nonconstant $J_n$-holomorphic spheres have energies at most $E_0$, and $x_n$ belongs to their images with $x_n\to x$, then some nonconstant component of their finite bubble-tree limit passes through $x$. The component may be the base sphere. The energy bound is essential to this statement's scope; no avoidance neighborhood for all energies at once, index formula, disk reflection, or degeneration count is asserted.

items.title: A real involution reflects boundary disks to holomorphic spheres
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a complex manifold with an antiholomorphic involution $R:X\to X$. Every smooth map $v:\overline{\mathbb D}\to X$ holomorphic in $\mathbb D$ and satisfying $v(\partial\mathbb D)\subset\operatorname{Fix}(R)$ extends to a holomorphic sphere by
$$V(z)=v(z)\quad(|z|\le1),\qquad V(z)=R\bigl(v(1/\overline z)\bigr)\quad(|z|\ge1).$$
The value at infinity is $R(v(0))$. If $v$ is nonconstant, this sphere is nonconstant and contains every boundary value of $v$.

In particular let $\Sigma$ be a connected closed Riemann surface with an antiholomorphic involution $\rho$, let $C_1,\ldots,C_{m+1}$ be pairwise disjoint embedded circles in its fixed set, and let
$$L=\{p_1+\cdots+p_m:p_i\in C_i\}\subset\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma),\qquad m\ge1.$$
For the standard complex symmetric-product structure, every smooth holomorphic closed disk with boundary on $L$ is constant, and no nonconstant holomorphic sphere intersects $L$.

The real Riemann surface and fixed circles are supplied hypotheses. Their existence for a given diagram, compatibility with all its auxiliary charts, regularity for perturbed structures, and deformation-invariant disk counts are separate assertions. For balanced $m=h+k-1$ this result does not assert the existence of $m+1$ real ovals when $k>1$.

items.title: An empty boundary-disk model remains empty at bounded energy
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be a compact smooth manifold, $L\subset X$ a compact embedded submanifold totally real for a smooth almost complex structure $J_0$. Suppose every smooth $J_0$-holomorphic closed disk with boundary on $L$ is constant and no nonconstant $J_0$-holomorphic sphere intersects $L$. Fix $E_0<\infty$.

There is a $C^\infty$ neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of $J_0$ such that every smooth almost complex structure $J\in\mathcal U$ satisfying the full endomorphism equality $J(x)=J_0(x)$ at every $x\in L$ has no nonconstant smooth $J$-holomorphic closed disk with boundary on $L$ and energy at most $E_0$. One may impose additional auxiliary constraints by intersection with this neighborhood.

In particular, for the supplied real-oval product torus in the disk-reflection theorem, the standard complex symmetric-product structure has such a neighborhood for every prescribed finite $E_0$. This does not construct the real model for arbitrary diagrams or provide one neighborhood for all energies. The conclusion is actual emptiness under the stated fixed-boundary condition, not a general deformation-invariance assertion for disk counts.

items.title: Boundary maps of finite planar hole domains extend with prescribed collars
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For $a=0,1$ let
$$P_a=D_{a,0}\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^r\operatorname{int}D_{a,i}\subset\mathbb R^2,$$
where every $D_{a,i}$ is the closed bounded region of a smooth embedded circle, the inner disks are pairwise disjoint, and each lies in the interior of the outer disk $D_{a,0}$. The number $r$ is finite and may be zero. Give $P_a$ the plane orientation. After any chosen labeling of the inner boundary components, let $b_i:\partial D_{0,i}\to\partial D_{1,i}$ be smooth diffeomorphisms all preserving their induced boundary orientations, or all reversing them, $0\le i\le r$.

There is a smooth diffeomorphism $B:P_0\to P_1$ extending all $b_i$, preserving orientation in the first case and reversing it in the second. Moreover, for any specified inward smooth collars $c_{a,i}$ of these boundary components into $P_a$, it may satisfy
$$B(c_{0,i}(p,t))=c_{1,i}(b_i(p),t)$$
for every $i$ and all sufficiently small $t\ge0$, with one common smaller collar width. No parametrization of either hole domain or general classification of smooth surfaces is an additional hypothesis or an imported conclusion.
items.scope_note: Actualfiniteplanardiskregionswithsmoothboundaries, disjointholes, consistentboundaryorientation sign and suppliedcollars. No arbitrarysurfaceclassification, no realmodelalreadyconstructed or integrabilityfrommetric claim.

items.title: A complete single-system Heegaard cut admits a real complex model
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $U$ be an oriented smooth handlebody with boundary $\Sigma$, and let $D_1,\ldots,D_h$, $h\ge1$, be disjoint proper compression disks whose cut manifold, after the usual collar rounding, is an actual smooth ball. Write $\alpha_i=\partial D_i$. Let $\beta$ be any finite disjoint union of smooth embedded circles transverse to the $\alpha_i$; it may in particular be the disjoint second attaching system of a singly pointed Heegaard diagram.

There are an orientation-compatible Riemann surface structure $j$ on the actual surface $\Sigma$, a smooth antiholomorphic involution $\rho$, and one further embedded circle $\delta$ such that
$$\operatorname{Fix}(\rho)=\alpha_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\alpha_h\sqcup\delta.$$
At every $\alpha$–$\beta$ crossing there is a $j$-holomorphic coordinate taking the local $\alpha$ arc to the real line and the local $\beta$ arc to the imaginary line. These crossing charts can be chosen with disjoint closures. Thus at every generator of two transverse product tori in $\operatorname{Sym}^h(\Sigma)$, their actual standard complex product chart has $T_\alpha=\mathbb R^h$ and $T_\beta=i\mathbb R^h$ locally.

For this standard symmetric-product structure no nonconstant holomorphic sphere intersects $T_\alpha$, and every smooth holomorphic closed disk with boundary on $T_\alpha$ is constant. For each prescribed finite energy bound this disk emptiness persists in a sufficiently small smooth neighborhood among structures equal to the standard structure as full endomorphisms on $T_\alpha$.

This constructs a model for ONE complete attaching system with $h$ disks cutting to ONE ball. It does not construct a common real model fixing two transverse attaching systems, assert an empty disk model for $T_\beta$ with this same $j$, provide $h+k$ real ovals for multipointed $k>1$, or prove general degeneration counts, their deformation invariance or Floer invariance.

items.title: Integrable boundary disks with zero-one domains have dense injective points
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a connected closed Riemann surface, let $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m$, $m\ge1$, be disjoint smooth embedded circles, and put $L=q(\gamma_1\times\cdots\times\gamma_m)\subset\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$. Let $u:\overline{\mathbb D}\to\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ be smooth, holomorphic in the interior for the standard complex structure, with boundary on $L$. For a component $R$ of $\Sigma\setminus\bigcup_i\gamma_i$, let $n_R(u)$ be its actual relative divisor-intersection degree, evaluated at any point of $R$.

If $u$ is nonconstant and $n_R(u)\in\{0,1\}$ for every $R$, then the set
$$I(u)=\{z\in\mathbb D:du(z)\ne0,\ u^{-1}(u(z))=\{z\}\text{ in }\overline{\mathbb D}\}$$
is open and dense in $\mathbb D$. In particular this applies to every nonconstant integrable disk whose actual domain is one cut component with coefficient one and zero on the others.

This is an integrable zero-one-domain statement. It neither factors arbitrary disks nor asserts that all index-two disks have such domains, that a perturbed almost complex disk automatically has dense injective points, or that the resulting moduli space is regular or has a specified count.

items.title: Proper unit-domain boundary disks are compact modulo node-fixing affine maps
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix a closed connected Riemann surface $\Sigma$, $m\ge1$ disjoint smooth attaching circles $\gamma_i$, and $L=q(\gamma_1\times\cdots\times\gamma_m)\subset X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$. Assume their complement has at least two components $A_1,\ldots,A_k$, and fix one of them, $A_i$. Fix a metric and surface area form and the diagonal and component-divisor neighborhoods of the compact-bubble energy theorem. Let smooth autonomous nearly symmetric structures $J_n\to J_\infty$ converge smoothly with this common geometry and with the full restrictions $J_n|_L=J_\infty|_L$ fixed.

Let $v_n:\overline{\mathbb D}\to X$ be smooth holomorphic disks for $J_n$, with boundary on $L$, whose actual component domains are precisely $A_i$ with coefficient one and zero on every other $A_j$. Mark one fixed source boundary point $p$. Suppose $v_n(p)=x_n\to x\in L$. Then there are orientation-preserving conformal disk automorphisms $g_n$ fixing $p$ and a nonconstant $J_\infty$-holomorphic smooth disk $v$ of the same unit domain, with $v(p)=x$, such that after a subsequence
$$v_n\circ g_n\longrightarrow v\quad\text{in }C^\infty(\overline{\mathbb D}).$$
In an upper-half-plane coordinate with $p=\infty$, these $g_n$ are exactly positive affine maps $z\mapsto a_nz+b_n$, $a_n>0$, $b_n\in\mathbb R$. No energy bound need be imposed on the sequence separately: the fixed unit domain gives one.

For a fixed such $J$ and fixed node value $x$, if every actual disk of this domain has surjective node-fixed linearization of real Fredholm index two, then there are only finitely many of their affine orbits. This proves compactness and conditional finiteness for proper unit domains; it supplies neither that index/surjectivity assertion nor the value of the resulting count.

items.title: Balanced attaching cuts admit round-component complex models
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $U$ be a connected oriented smooth handlebody with connected boundary $\Sigma$ of genus $h$, and let $m=h+k-1>0$ disjoint proper compression disks cut it into $k$ actual smooth balls. Write $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m$ for their boundary circles. Let $\beta$ be a finite disjoint union of smooth circles transverse to the $\gamma_i$.

There is an orientation-compatible Riemann surface structure $j$ on the actual $\Sigma$ such that each component of its surface cut along the $\gamma_i$ is conformally an explicit Riemann sphere with finitely many pairwise disjoint round disk interiors removed. This conformal identification is smooth up to every boundary circle. Each $\gamma$–$\beta$ crossing has a $j$-holomorphic coordinate in which those two arcs are precisely the real and imaginary lines. The finitely many crossing charts can have disjoint closures.

Consequently every transverse product-torus generator in $\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ has an actual standard product-integrable chart with $T_\gamma=\mathbb R^m$ and $T_\beta=i\mathbb R^m$ locally. In particular a specified generator has a standard complex chart flattening $T_\gamma$ without changing the standard symmetric-product structure there.

This is an auxiliary complex-model construction for the full balanced disk count geometry. It asserts no antiholomorphic involution, additional real ovals, disk emptiness, boundary index or count, transversality or invariance.

items.title: Near-integrable proper unit-domain disks have free injective sites
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix the symmetric-product geometry, disjoint attaching circles and torus $L$ of the proper unit-domain disk compactness theorem, with at least two attaching-system complement components. Let $J_0=\operatorname{Sym}^m(j)$ be the standard integrable structure. Let $D\subset X$ be a compact protected neighborhood of the diagonal and the finitely many chosen component and marked divisors, disjoint from $L$. Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N$ be pairwise disjoint compact generator neighborhoods disjoint from $D$, each contained in a $J_0$-holomorphic chart which takes $L$ exactly to the real plane. Set
$$P=D\cup L\cup\bigcup_{a=1}^N A_a.$$
The working fixed generator charts may lie inside the interiors of the $A_a$. These chart hypotheses can be supplied by the balanced round-component construction.

Among the smooth autonomous nearly symmetric structures with this fixed geometry and equal to $J_0$ as full endomorphisms on $L$, $D$ and the $A_a$, there is a $C^\infty$ neighborhood of $J_0$ such that every actual smooth holomorphic disk of any proper unit component domain has a point $z\in\mathbb D$ satisfying
$$du(z)\ne0,\qquad u^{-1}(u(z))=\{z\}\text{ in }\overline{\mathbb D},\qquad u(z)\notin P.$$
Such points form a nonempty open source set. This holds without imposing a boundary node value; in particular it holds for every disk with any specified node value on $L$.

The result proves one free injective site for these actual nearby disks. It does not assert dense injective points for arbitrary perturbed disks, surjectivity of their linearizations, an index formula, a degeneration count or gluing.

items.title: Near-integrable proper unit-domain disks are generically node-fixed regular
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the standard integrable background, protected spatial sets $D,A_x,L$ and nearly symmetric geometric class of the free-injective-site theorem, with at least two attaching-system complement components and with finitely many node values $x\in L$ inside smaller working exact charts in $\operatorname{Int}A_x$. Require the optional taming hypothesis of the disk-variation theorem whenever tameness is part of the geometric class.

There is an actual separable Hilbert ball of smooth autonomous nearly symmetric structures $J(a)$ near the standard background, preserving all values on $D\cup L\cup\bigcup_xA_x$ and the working charts, such that a dense residual subset of parameters has this property simultaneously for all the prescribed node values: EVERY actual disk of any proper unit component domain, with boundary on $L$ and that marked boundary value, has surjective actual compact node-fixed $H^3\to H^2$ linearization. It is also surjective in every actual weighted node-fixed realization of weight $0<\delta<\pi$ and every integer order. At every such disk the actual universal derivative is onto.

No dense-injective-point hypothesis on the perturbed disk is imposed: the open free injective site is proved by the compactness and integrable unit-domain suppliers. This establishes regularity only. It does not compute the node-fixed index or the count value, classify arbitrary higher-domain degenerations, or give attachment gluing and cancellation.

items.title: A proper round disk component has boundary-degeneration count one
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use an actual balanced round-component complex model, with $m>0$ attaching circles $\gamma_j$, product torus $L$, at least two cut components, and standard integrable structure $J_0$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$. Suppose one proper cut component $A$ has exactly ONE boundary component, a single copy of $\gamma_i$. Its closure is the round disk complementary to the assigned round disk face in its sphere chart. Fix a node tuple $x=x_1+\cdots+x_m\in L$, $x_j\in\gamma_j$, and one marked source boundary point $p$.

The standard smooth holomorphic closed disks with node value $x$, actual component domain $A$ with coefficient one and zero elsewhere, have exactly ONE orbit under orientation-preserving conformal disk automorphisms fixing $p$. Their actual compact node-fixed linearization is surjective of real Fredholm index two, with kernel precisely the two infinitesimal node-fixing automorphisms. The same surjectivity and index hold in every actual weighted node-fixed realization of weight $0<\delta<\pi$ and every order when the protected exact node charts are used.

Take the actual smooth Hilbert family of protected structures based at $J_0$ in the proper-unit-domain regularity theorem, with $x$ among its prescribed node values. On a sufficiently small parameter ball, EVERY parameter has exactly one such disk orbit and it remains regular of index two in the same realizations. Thus its actual finite count modulo two is one. The radius may be chosen simultaneously for any finite list of such disk components and node tuples.

This computes the one-boundary-component base case only. It does not reduce a general component with several boundary circles to this case, compute its count, or supply target degeneration, attachment gluing, cancellation or Floer invariance.

items.title: A round disk boundary attachment has an explicit regular strip family
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the proper one-boundary-component disk $A$, standard integrable structure and whole-image product chart of the round disk count theorem. Let $x$ be an actual transverse generator of two disjoint attaching systems, with $A$ bounded by $\gamma_i$ in the first system. Use the balanced round-component construction so that the second-system arc through $x_i$ is radial in the round disk coordinate near that boundary point and all inactive crossing lines are orthogonal. Let $\chi$ take $\overline A$ to the closed unit disk and $x_i$ to one, and put $W=i(1-\chi)/(1+\chi)$, taking $A$ to the upper half-plane and $x_i$ to zero.

For all sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$ there is an actual smooth finite-energy standard holomorphic strip $u_\epsilon:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ with both ends $x$, first-system boundary at $t=0$, second-system boundary at $t=1$, and actual domain $A$. Its inactive coordinates are the other $x_j$, and its active coordinate is exactly
$$W(u_\epsilon(s,t))=-\frac{\epsilon}{\sinh(\pi(s+it)/2)}.$$
The pole at $(s,t)=(0,0)$ is interpreted in the smooth target coordinate $\chi$, where the value is $-1$.

Every $u_\epsilon$ has surjective actual fixed-end linearization of real index two before translation. Its kernel is precisely the span of $\partial_su_\epsilon$ and $\partial_\epsilon u_\epsilon$. These assertions hold at every Sobolev order and at weights $0\le\delta<\pi/2$. The two parameters consisting of translation and $\epsilon$ give the full local regular zero chart at each positive $\epsilon$.

As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, the strip converges smoothly to the constant strip $x$ away from $(0,0)$. In the source rescaling $s+it=(2\epsilon/\pi)\zeta$ it converges smoothly on compact subsets of the closed upper half-plane to the disk $W=-1/\zeta$, with its smooth target value at $\zeta=0$ and node at infinity. That disk is the unique orbit of the unit-domain disk in the count theorem. The strip energies equal its energy, so this degeneration loses no energy.

This is an exact integrable boundary-attachment family with proved local regularity. It does not yet assert that every strip approaching this nodal limit lies in this family, that the family persists uniformly down to $\epsilon=0$ for perturbed structures, or that arbitrary boundary components reduce to this case.

items.title: The integrable round disk attachment exhausts its nodal limit
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the standard integrable proper round disk component $A$, actual transverse generator $x$, radial second-system crossing germ, and whole-image ordered product chart of the explicit boundary-attachment theorem. Thus $\chi(\overline A)=\overline{\mathbb D}$, $\chi(x_i)=1$, and $W=i(1-\chi)/(1+\chi)$. Take the inactive coordinate disks small enough that their first-system arcs are real lines, their second-system crossing germs are imaginary lines, and they are disjoint from $\overline A$ and one another.

Every nonconstant smooth finite-energy standard holomorphic strip of actual domain $A$, with both ends $x$, whose full closed image lies in this ordered product chart and whose entire upper boundary lies in the specified product crossing germ, is exactly
$$u(s,t)=u_\epsilon(s-b,t),\qquad \epsilon>0,\quad b\in\mathbb R,$$
where $u_\epsilon$ is the explicit family and its upper edge lies in that germ. Both parameters are unique. Its actual regularity and index are those of that family.

In particular suppose a bounded-energy sequence of such standard domain-$A$ strips has an actual bubbled-strip limit, after longitudinal translation, consisting of the constant strip $x$ and precisely the unique unit-domain disk attached at $(0,0)$. Require the actual smooth core convergence and connecting-annulus and outer-tail image collapse supplied by bubbled-strip compactness; there are no other nonconstant components. No whole-image-chart or upper-germ assumption on the sequence is needed here. Eventually every strip belongs to the displayed family, with $\epsilon_n\to0$ and $b_n\to0$. Thus the exact integrable family exhausts this nodal limit.

This proves exhaustion for this integrable disk-component model. It does not supply uniform gluing for perturbed structures, count or factor a many-boundary component, or classify all low-index boundary strata.
items.scope_note: Exact standard integrable one-boundary-component basecase only. Actual sequential nodal exhaustion, not uniform perturbed inverse/gluing.

items.title: Near-integrable proper unit-domain disk counts are finite and deformation invariant
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the actual balanced round-component integrable model and the protected autonomous Hilbert family $J(a)$ of the proper-unit-domain generic regularity theorem, with finitely many fixed node values in its working exact charts. There are at least two attaching-system cut components. Supply finite smooth triangulations of their planar closures as in the integrable planar index theorem.

After shrinking its parameter ball, EVERY actual disk of a proper unit component domain, at any of those nodes and any parameter, has compact node-fixed $H^3\to H^2$ Fredholm index two. Its weighted node-fixed index is also two at every integer order and weight $0<\delta<\pi$. For every parameter at which all these disks are regular, each domain and node has finitely many positive-affine orbits. Such parameters include a dense residual subset of the ball.

For any two such regular parameters, the orbit counts modulo two agree separately for every prescribed node and every proper unit component domain. More precisely there is an actual smooth path between them, staying in this one ball, whose parametrized disk orbit spaces are compact smooth one-manifolds with boundary the two endpoint orbit sets.

This defines and proves local deformation invariance of the actual counts. It does not compute their value for a component with several boundary circles, assert existence of its disks, classify higher domains, or give disk attachment or target degeneration gluing.

items.title: Round disk incidence position is a global matching coordinate
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the proper round one-boundary-component disk $A$, node tuple $x$, and actual protected parameter family of the disk-component count theorem, restricted to its sufficiently small ball. Choose the protected component point $y\in A$, disjoint from the attaching curves, so that every structure equals the standard structure on a fixed neighborhood of $E_y=\{y\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}\Sigma$. Identify the marked source disk minus its node with the upper half-plane $\mathbb H$, with that node at infinity.

For every parameter $a$, let $\mathcal M_a$ be the actual smooth node-fixed holomorphic disks of domain $A$, before quotienting by positive affine automorphisms. Every such disk meets $E_y$ at exactly one interior source point, with intersection multiplicity one; write that point $\rho_a(u)\in\mathbb H$. Then
$$\rho_a:\mathcal M_a\longrightarrow\mathbb H$$
is a smooth diffeomorphism. The maps and their inverses depend smoothly on $a$ in the actual local solution charts, and
$$\rho_a(u\circ g)=g^{-1}\rho_a(u),\qquad g(z)=cz+d,\quad c>0.$$

At each disk, the actual augmented linearization consisting of its compact node-fixed operator and the derivative of this incidence position is a bounded isomorphism
$$(P_u,d\rho_u):H^3_{\partial L,\,p=0}\longrightarrow H^2\oplus\mathbb R^2.$$
The same assertion holds at higher integer realizations $H^{q+1}\to H^q$ for $q\ge2$, and for their actual weighted node-fixed realizations of weight $0<\delta<\pi$. Point evaluation on an ordinary $H^1$ domain is not asserted.

This is an actual disk-side incidence matching model for the one-boundary-component case. It does not supply the target-neck gluing or its exhaustion theorem, nor reduce a general attaching component to a disk.

items.title: Round planar boundary pole kernels have a unique positive period kernel
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $A$ be the open interior of a bounded round disk with finitely many pairwise disjoint round CLOSED disks removed, all strictly inside the outer disk. Let its $e\ge1$ boundary circles be $\Gamma_j$, and choose $x_j\in\Gamma_j$. For each $j$ choose a real-circle Möbius coordinate $w_j$ taking $x_j$ to zero and the side of $A$ locally to the upper half-plane.

There is a unique real harmonic function $P_j$ on $A$ which is smooth up to every boundary point except $x_j$, vanishes there, and has
$$P_j=\operatorname{Im}(-1/w_j)+v_j$$
near $x_j$, with $v_j$ harmonic and smooth across that boundary arc and zero on the arc. It is strictly positive in $A$. Define $C_{ij}$ for $i\ne j$ as the outward flux $\int_{\Gamma_i}\partial_\nu P_j\,ds$. Define $C_{jj}$ as the flux across any nearby interior parallel of $\Gamma_j$, with normal pointing toward $\Gamma_j$. Then
$$C_{ij}<0\quad(i\ne j),\qquad \sum_iC_{ij}=0.$$
The latter diagonal flux is finite and independent of the parallel. The real matrix $C$ has rank $e-1$. Its kernel is generated by a vector with every entry strictly positive, uniquely normalized by $\sum_jc_j=1$.

Consequently $H=\sum_jc_jP_j$ is a positive harmonic function with one prescribed positive simple boundary pole at each $x_j$ and zero flux around every boundary component. Every harmonic function vanishing on the boundary apart from simple poles at these points, with the same local type and zero boundary periods, is a real multiple of $H$. The last uniqueness permits arbitrary real residues; positivity makes that multiple positive for a nonzero nonnegative function.

This supplies actual harmonic kernels and their finite period equation. It asserts no holomorphic proper-cover or symmetric-product disk construction by itself.
items.scope_note: Actual finite boundedroundholeddomain andmarkedboundarypoints; finite realmatrixperiod equation only. No generalAi internalpairedcircle reduction, holomorphiccover or Floerdisk construction asserted.

items.title: Planar components without internal attaching pairs have boundary count one
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the balanced round-component integrable model with $m$ disjoint attaching circles, product torus $L$, at least two cut components, and a fixed node tuple $x\in L$. Let $A$ be a proper planar cut component with a supplied finite smooth triangulation. Suppose NO attaching circle has both of its boundary copies on $A$. Thus its $e\ge1$ boundary circles have distinct labels, and every other labelled circle is disjoint from $\overline A$.

For the standard integrable structure, the actual smooth disks of unit component domain $A$, with boundary on $L$ and the prescribed boundary node $x$, form exactly ONE orbit under the positive affine automorphisms fixing that node. They exist, and their actual compact node-fixed $H^3\to H^2$ linearizations are onto of real index two, with kernel precisely the two affine directions. The same regularity and index hold in every higher and actual weighted realization with $0<\delta<\pi$.

For the actual protected nearly symmetric Hilbert family based at this integrable model, every parameter in a sufficiently small ball likewise has exactly one such disk orbit, regular of index two. Its mod-two count is therefore one. A common ball works for finitely many nodes and components satisfying the stated no-internal-pair condition.

This treats any number of external boundary circles. It does not remove an internal paired attaching circle, compute the count for a component with such a pair, or supply target-neck or boundary-attachment gluing.

items.title: A finite real-boundary Cauchy--Riemann neck has an explicit zero-mode inverse
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $R>0$, $m\ge1$, and $C_R=[0,R]\times[0,1]$. Consider $D_0=\partial_s+i\partial_t$ on $\mathbb C^m$-valued $H^1$ sections with real zeroth traces on $t=0,1$. Use the real orthonormal modes $\phi_n(t)=e^{-i\pi nt}$, $n\in\mathbb Z$, coordinatewise, and let $a_n(s)$ be the real mode coefficients. Impose the mixed spectral conditions
$$a_n(0)=0\ (n>0),\qquad a_n(R)=0\ (n<0),\qquad a_0(0)=0.$$
These define a closed Hilbert subspace $X_R$ of $H^1(C_R)$ using actual weak traces, without extra forcing-edge conditions. Then
$$D_0:X_R\longrightarrow L^2(C_R;\mathbb C^m)$$
is a bounded real isomorphism. Writing $f_n$ for the real coefficients of $f$, its inverse is
$$a_n(s)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\int_0^s e^{-\pi n(s-r)}f_n(r)\,dr,&n>0,\\\displaystyle-\int_s^R e^{-\pi n(s-r)}f_n(r)\,dr,&n<0,\\\displaystyle\int_0^s f_0(r)\,dr,&n=0.\end{cases}$$
The nonzero-mode inverse has $H^1$ norm bounded independently of $R$. The full inverse satisfies
$$\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(1+R)\|f\|_{L^2},$$
with $C$ independent of $R$, and its zero mode has the exact drift
$$a_0(R)-a_0(0)=\int_0^R f_0(r)\,dr.$$
Allowing a specified real initial constant $c$ adds precisely the constant section $c$; its $H^1$ norm is $\sqrt R|c|$. Requiring instead both zero-mode end values to vanish gives zero kernel and the closed range $\int_0^R f_0=0$, of real codimension $m$, with the same inverse bound on that range.

This is a finite-neck weak $H^1\to L^2$ operator statement. It asserts no unrestricted higher-order corner regularity, uniform bound for the zero mode as $R\to\infty$, geometric parametrix or nonlinear gluing.
items.scope_note: FiniteRRcylinder H1→L2 only; no unrestrictedHqcornerregularity, no uniformzero-modebound, no gluedgeometricoperator or nonlinearattachmenttheorem claimed.

items.title: Real-boundary node caps have bounded incoming--outgoing response maps
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Consider either the actual constant transverse strip with one boundary node, or the actual generator-punctured nonconstant autonomous boundary disk. Use their exact node coordinate $\zeta=\sigma+i\tau$, $\sigma\ge0$, $0\le\tau\le1$, with actual operator $D_0=\partial_\sigma+i\partial_\tau$ and real boundary planes on both edges. In the disk case assume its actual compact node-fixed linearization is onto of real index two. Fix any $0<\delta<\pi$.

In the disk case choose two bounded compact-core real phases whose restriction to the affine kernel is invertible. Remove the end beyond a fixed sufficiently large $S$; the remaining source is the cap. In the strip case its two original ends still have fixed zero limits. Let
$$G_-=\{(g_n)_{n<0}:g_n\in\mathbb R^m,\ \sum_{n<0}(1+|n|)|g_n|^2<\infty\},$$
and define $G_+$ similarly for $n>0$. Use $\phi_n(\tau)=e^{-i\pi n\tau}$ and the actual weak $H^1$ trace at $\sigma=S$.

For the strip cap, every incoming negative trace $g\in G_-$ has exactly one homogeneous cap solution with that trace, the real physical boundary conditions and its original zero ends. Its trace is
$$g+A_cg+E_cg,\qquad A_c:G_-\to G_+,\quad E_c:G_-\to\mathbb R^m,$$
with bounded linear response maps. For the disk cap, every incoming $g\in G_-$ and every real constant mode $c$ have exactly one homogeneous cap solution with these traces and zero phases. Its trace is
$$g+A_dg+B_dc+c,$$
where $A_d:G_-\to G_+$ and $B_d:\mathbb R^m\to G_+$ are bounded. All solution maps into cap $H^1$ are bounded.

Moreover $A_c,E_c,A_d$ are norm limits of their finite incoming-mode truncations, with error at most $Ce^{-\pi N}$ after retaining the modes $-1,\ldots,-N$. Their construction uses actual node inverses; no general Calderon projector or arbitrary-choice compactness theorem is a premise. This does not yet sew two caps through a finite neck or prove nonlinear gluing.

items.title: Constant strip and regular disk sewing has a controlled linear neck inverse
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Take the actual constant-strip cap and regular node-fixed index-two disk cap, with phases and exact real-boundary collars, of the cap response theorem. Sew their cut circles by a real-boundary cylinder $[0,T]\times[0,1]$. At its right end use the disk coordinate with the reflected transverse parameter $\tau_d=1-t$ and reversed longitudinal parameter, so the coordinate change is holomorphic. Identify their vector bundles by their common exact node frame and use the actual Cauchy--Riemann symbol transformation on forcings. Let $P_T$ equal the actual component operators on the fixed caps and $D_0$ on this cylinder; these coincide on their exact collar overlaps.

Use weak $H^1$ sections with the actual zeroth physical real boundary traces, fixed zero limits at the original strip ends, and matched traces at the seams. Impose the two fixed compact disk-core phases to be zero. Use the sum of fixed-cap and ordinary-cylinder Sobolev square norms, with fixed collar overlaps; the constant mode on the finite cylinder is part of that ordinary function norm. For all sufficiently large $T$, the actual sewn operator is a bounded isomorphism
$$P_T:X_T^{\ell=0,H^1}\longrightarrow Y_T^{L^2},\qquad \|P_T^{-1}\|\le C(1+T).$$
Without the two phases it is onto with two-dimensional kernel and real Fredholm index two. For each fixed integer $q\ge0$, the same inverse maps the actual $H^q$ target to $H^{q+1}$ sections, with only the original zeroth physical traces and phases, and
$$\|P_T^{-1}f\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q(1+T)\|f\|_{H^q}.$$
The constants are independent of sufficiently large $T$. No extra normal trace or forcing-edge condition is imposed.

This is a sewn geometric linear operator, not yet nonlinear holomorphic-disk attachment. If the strip node is $z=0$ and the punctured disk coordinate is $w=-1/\zeta$, the source plumbing $zw=-\epsilon$ with fixed cut radius $r$ realizes this sewn surface as the actual original strip: the disk core has coordinate $z=\epsilon\zeta$ and the neck length is $T=\pi^{-1}\log(r^2/\epsilon)$. No uniformization theorem is used in this identification.
